function: Configuring the discrete RIS phase shifts to maximize the multiuser downlink sum rate (p. 2, Eq. 9).
system: 4-antenna femtocell BS, 2 single-antenna users, 10x10 reflecting RIS with 1-bit phase shifts, indoor room, 5.25 GHz, 10 MHz bandwidth (pp. 2, 4, 5).
method: Double deep Q-network with column-wise accumulated actions plus a greedy element-wise refinement inside each step; reinforcement learning (pp. 1, 3).
data_channel: Custom simulated indoor Rician channels: LoS from the ITU-R P.1238 loss model, i.i.d. NLoS, Rician factor 5, random positions; no dataset (p. 4).
test_conditions: Training and test are not separated: sum rates come from training curves over random scenario setups; RIS size varied from 8x8 to 16x16 (pp. 4-5).
baselines: Non-learned: flat phases, random phases, PSO then quantization. Learned: column-wise DQN [3] and column-wise DDQN [8] (p. 4).
metrics: Sum rate in Mbps (training curves and versus RIS size), DRL action-space size (pp. 3-5).
complexity: Big-O order O(IT((1+1/Nf) sum of nl*nl-1 + P*V)) for DDQN plus greedy search; action space grows as square root of N (pp. 1, 4).
q1_support: p. 4: "adopting the ITU LoS" basic transmission loss model; the NLoS parts are i.i.d. Custom Rician simulator that takes only the LoS path loss from ITU-R P.1238; no 3GPP, DeepMIMO, or measured data.
q2_support: p. 4: "Other training parameters are shown in Table I for a 10 × 10 RIS." The RIS-size sweep (p. 5, Fig. 3c) is a sweep in the same simulator; no test in unseen conditions, no transfer or fine-tuning is stated.
q3_support: p. 5: "and 24% higher than DQN." Non-learned: p. 4: "then quantize to discrete values." (PSO), plus random and flat. DQN [3] and DDQN [8] are earlier learned RIS designs, compared on sum rate (Fig. 3b-c).
q4_support: p. 4: "process has a complexity of O(V ), the overall embedded GA" in Section III-C, Complexity Analysis, which gives the total order of the proposed algorithm.
q5_support: p. 4: "components are assumed to be independently and identically" distributed; channels are simulated. No code or data link and no public channel dataset appear in the 5 pages.
notes: PDF is the arXiv v1 preprint (arXiv:2505.04401) and carries no DOI; it is identified by its title and topic. q1 is 0 because ITU-R P.1238 supplies only the LoS path loss inside a custom Rician model; the reviewer may confirm this reading. q2 is 0 because the paper never tests a trained model on a condition it was not trained on; the state and action sizes depend on N (p. 2-3), so Fig. 3c most likely uses one training per RIS size, which the paper does not say. q3 counts column-wise DQN [3], an earlier published learned RIS phase design, as the learned baseline; the DDQN baseline [8] is a standard algorithm on the same problem.
